# Results — Study 684 (Inverted Hammer) on the real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One recipe — detect the
**inverted-hammer** geometry (small body at the bottom of the range, upper wick ≥ 2× the
body, little/no lower shadow) by precise OHLC rules across the same fixed basket of **26**
liquid US large-caps + SPY used by the sibling candlestick studies (yfinance **un-adjusted,
price-only** daily bars), split by **prior 10-day trend** into the bullish claim under test
(shape after a **downtrend**, traded **long**), measure the **forward 1/3/5/10-day return**
entered at the **next close** (one execution lag) against each name's **unconditional base
rate**, and run a HAC one-sample *t* + a label-shuffle placebo + a **Bonferroni** correction
across the four-horizon family. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month).*

## Data stamp

- **Basket** (26, survivors, same panel as 403-hammer-hanging-man / 404-shooting-star): SPY,
  AAPL, MSFT, JNJ, PG, KO, JPM, WMT, XOM, CVX, PFE, MRK, INTC, CSCO, HD, MCD, DIS, BA, CAT,
  MMM, HON, UNH, ORCL, PEP, COST, GS.
- **Span**: 1962-01-02 → 2026-06-30 · **345,846** daily bars · **10,735** inverted-hammer-
  shaped bars (any trend context).
- **Adjustment**: un-adjusted OHLC (the candle *shape* needs the printed levels); forward
  returns are therefore **price-only** (no dividends).
- **Content fingerprint** (panel, close columns over the basket): `8ddaab4e2e1e`. Companion
  single-name stamp (SPY OHLC, `quantlab.repro.data_stamp`): `7987ab25910e`
  (8,411 rows, 1993-01-29 → 2026-06-30).
- **Survivorship**: a fixed surviving-names basket — for this **bullish** claim the bias
  points *toward* finding a bounce (survivors recovered from dips that delisted names did
  not), so a null/weak result is **conservative**. Named on the Signal axis.
- **Multiple testing**: the same claim is tested across **four horizons** (1/3/5/10 days) —
  a Bonferroni correction (`p_adj = min(1, p_raw × 4)`) is reported next to the raw
  label-shuffle *p* for every horizon, not just the best one.

## The headline — INVERTED HAMMER (shape after a downtrend), traded LONG, gross & net

The folk recipe: a long upper wick after a slide shows sellers running out of room — buy
the bounce. Edge = conditional mean minus that name's base rate; net = gross − 2 × 5 bps
round trip (long-only, no borrow).

| Horizon | n | cond % | base % | **edge %** | win % | **HAC *t*** | placebo *p* | Bonferroni *p* | net % |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 day  | 4,895 | +0.104 | +0.066 | **+0.045** | 49.4 | **+1.45** | 0.042 | 0.166 | −0.055 |
| 3 days | 4,895 | +0.272 | +0.196 | **+0.095** | 52.2 | **+1.79** | 0.021 | 0.082 | −0.005 |
| 5 days | 4,894 | +0.397 | +0.324 | **+0.105** | 52.6 | **+1.49** | 0.035 | 0.142 | +0.005 |
| 10 days| 4,891 | +0.714 | +0.639 | **+0.137** | 55.7 | **+1.48** | 0.046 | 0.185 | +0.037 |

- The inverted hammer's **best** edge is **+0.095% at 3 days, HAC *t* = +1.79** — a real but
  *sub-bar* tilt: it clears the raw label-shuffle placebo at the 5% level (*p* = 0.021) but
  **never reaches *t* ≥ 2**, and once the four-horizon family is Bonferroni-corrected, every
  horizon's adjusted *p* is **≥ 0.082** — none survive.
- Win-rate creeps above 50% only at 3-10 days (52-56%) — a small, drift-sized tilt, not a
  reliable coin-flip beater.

## The bearish-context contrast — SAME geometry after an UPTREND (traded long as a myth-check)

If the pattern is genuinely trend-conditional, buying the identical geometry on the
**wrong** side of the trend split (after an uptrend — the shooting-star context, sibling
study [404](../../404-shooting-star/)) should show a *weaker or negative* tilt.

| Horizon | n | edge (bps) | win % | HAC *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 day  | 5,673 | +3.3 | 49.6 | +1.48 | 0.093 |
| 3 days | 5,673 | +4.5 | 51.6 | +1.12 | 0.151 |
| 5 days | 5,673 | +6.5 | 53.0 | +1.21 | 0.115 |
| 10 days| 5,669 | −0.5 | 53.3 | −0.07 | 0.530 |

The "wrong-side" long trade is smaller than the inverted-hammer edge at 1/3/5 days but the
*same sign* — the trend split does not clearly discriminate a floor from a continuation
drift; it mostly changes the size, not the direction, of a broadly positive tilt after this
wick shape. That is itself evidence against a genuinely trend-conditional reversal
mechanism, not for one.

## The geometry alone — ANY (pooling both trend contexts), traded long

| Horizon | n | edge (bps) | win % | HAC *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 day  | 10,735 | +3.9 | 49.5 | **+2.13** | 0.014 |
| 3 days | 10,735 | +6.9 | 51.8 | **+2.23** | 0.013 |
| 5 days | 10,734 | +8.3 | 52.8 | +1.97 | 0.016 |
| 10 days| 10,727 | +5.6 | 54.3 | +0.91 | 0.149 |

Pooling away the trend split (the largest sample, 10,735 events) is the *only* cut of the
data where the raw *t* touches +2 (1 and 3 days) — but Bonferroni over the same four-horizon
family brings the adjusted *p* to **0.056 / 0.052 / 0.064 / 0.596**, so it does not survive
family-wise correction either, and it is not even the claim under test (the folklore is
explicitly trend-conditional). Quoted here only to show the ceiling of what the geometry
alone can offer.

## Myth-check — does a deeper-washout or shorter-lookback filter rescue the floor? (H = 3)

| Variant | edge % | HAC *t* | placebo *p* | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| plain inverted hammer (trend lookback = 10) | +0.095 | +1.79 | 0.021 | 4,895 |
| trend lookback = 5 | +0.134 | **+2.64** | 0.002 | 4,906 |
| trend lookback = 20 | +0.077 | +1.41 | 0.045 | 4,785 |
| min prior washout ≥ 5% | +0.413 | **+2.85** | 0.000 | 1,265 |
| min prior washout ≥ 10% | +0.527 | +1.02 | 0.015 | 257 |
| stricter wick (≥ 3× body) | +0.072 | +0.94 | 0.137 | 2,486 |
| stricter wick (≥ 4× body) | +0.092 | +0.87 | 0.136 | 1,408 |

Two knobs *can* be tuned to push *t* above 2 (a shorter 5-day lookback, or requiring a ≥5%
prior washout) — but the "rescue" is not robust: doubling the washout threshold to 10%
**collapses** *t* back to 1.02 on a much thinner sample (257 events) instead of strengthening
monotonically, and demanding a *longer, purer* wick (the "textbook-perfect" inverted hammer)
**weakens** it (*t* ≈ 0.9) rather than confirming it. A signal that appears and disappears as
you dial the filter, with no consistent dose-response, is the signature of a snooped subset,
not a real effect (Sullivan-Timmermann-White 1999).

| cost (one-way bps) | net edge (bps) |
|---|--:|
| 0.0  | +9.5 |
| 1.0  | +7.5 |
| 5.0  | **−0.5** |
| 10.0 | −10.5 |

Break-even sits under ~2 bps one-way — far inside the bid-ask spread of any of these names.
At the desk's standard 5 bps one-way convention the *best* horizon is already net-negative.

**2 of 26 names** (CVX, CAT) individually clear |*t*| > 2 — right around the ~1.3 expected

history length (BA at −1.60 vs CVX at +2.26).

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery works when there's a floor to find

On a deterministic OHLC panel (`data.synthetic_panel`) where we **plant** a post-inverted-
hammer bounce, the same engine reads ≈ 0 with no edge and lights up hard when one exists:

| planted bounce | events | edge % | HAC *t* | placebo *p* | win % |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.000 (random walk) | 2,508 | +0.014 | +0.57 | 0.267 | 52.0 |
| 0.005 (real floor)  | 2,492 | +0.321 | **+12.78** | 0.000 | 61.4 |

Zero edge cannot fake significance (*t* = 0.57); a genuine 0.5%/event floor is detected at
*t* = 12.8. The flat-ish real-tape reading is therefore a genuine (near-)null, not a blind
harness — the pipeline can bank a planted signal when one is actually there.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The bullish claim's best real-tape statistic is **+0.095% at 3 days,
  HAC *t* = +1.79** — under the **t ≥ 2** bar, and once the four-horizon family is
  Bonferroni-corrected, no horizon's adjusted *p* clears 0.05 (best 0.082). Only **2 of 26**
  names individually cross |*t*| > 2 — chance-level. The identical geometry on the "wrong"
  side of the trend split (post-uptrend) shows the **same sign**, undercutting the
  trend-conditional reversal story itself. The harness detects a planted floor at
  *t* = 12.8, so the sub-bar reading is genuine. Survivorship tilts *toward* a bounce here,
  making this a conservative null.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Net of a 5-bps round trip the edge is **negative or a rounding
  error at every horizon** (−0.055% to +0.037%); break-even sits under ~2 bps one-way. The
  pattern's best horizon is already underwater at standard costs.
- **"Deeper washout rescues the floor?" — BUSTED.** A shorter trend lookback and a ≥5%
  washout filter can each push *t* above 2 on a thinned sample, but the effect is
  **non-monotonic** (a 10% washout threshold *collapses* it back to *t* = 1.02) and a
  *longer, purer* wick — the folklore's "stronger" signal — makes it **worse**
  (*t* ≈ 0.9). The pattern's apparent rescues are filter-snooping artefacts, not a
  dose-response a real effect would show.
